quotes.quote: Title: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
Authors: Ahmed Masry , Do Xuan Long , Jia Qing Tan , Shafiq Joty , Enamul Hoque
Accepted by ACL 2022 Findings
[Submitted on 19 Mar 2022]
In this work, we present a large-scale benchmark covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries.

existing datasets have several major limitations: (i) the questions are generated automatically using pre-defined templates … which lack naturalness, (ii) the charts are created automatically using a programming tool like Matplotlib … which do not reflect the diverse styles of many real-world charts
Our benchmark consists of 20,882 charts which are curated from four different online sources to ensure variety in visual styles and topics.
we crawled charts from four different sources: (i) Statista (statista.com) is an online platform that presents charts covering a variety of topics including economy, politics, and industry.
For the Pew dataset, we only crawled chart images since the underlying data tables are not available.

Compositional questions contain at least two mathematical/logical operations like sum, difference and average, while visual questions refer to the visual attributes such as color, height, and length of graphical marks (e.g., bars) in the chart.

We also evaluate the transferability of the models and the datasets, where we first pretrain the two top performing models (VisionTaPas and VL-T5) on the PlotQA dataset and then fine-tune them on ChartQA.
the performance of our models decreases when the gold data table was not given. This highlights the increasing challenge of automatic data extraction from real-world charts with diversity in styles.
While VisionTaPas and VL-T5 handle various mathematical/logical operations, still they cannot effectively handle nested operations.
Current approaches for automatic data extraction are modular and combine deep learning and rule-based methods which are error-prone.
Currently, our models take the data table and the visual features of the chart separately and then combine them. Such representation does not fully capture the chart structure.
